what: AT&T is one of the two largest mobile operators in the United States. It sells phone and data plans, and is building fibre broadband to replace its old copper network. It no longer owns a media business after spinning off WarnerMedia.
customers: US households and businesses buying mobile service, home internet and business connectivity.
money: postpaid and prepaid wireless service and device sales
legacy voice and data services to companies
moat: Spectrum licences and a national network that cost tens of billions to build, in a market with only three large operators.
risks: Debt of about $178 billion is among the largest of any US company
Legacy business wireline revenue keeps shrinking
Price competition from cable operators selling mobile service
Copper network retirement and fibre building need continuous capital
opportunities: Fibre broadband wins customers from cable and holds them longer
Mobile customers who also take fibre leave far less often
A dividend yield above 6% is now covered by free cash flow after the dividend cut
watch: Postpaid phone net additions and fibre customer growth.
